newsitem.title: ITALY: IMI to buy one pct of San Paolo.
newsitem.headline: IMI to buy one pct of San Paolo.

text.p: Italian investment bank IMI said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy a stake of around one percent in Italy's largest bank San Paolo di Torino as part of the Turin-based bank's privatisation programme.
An IMI statement after a group board meeting said that the investment bank would hold the shares for a "period of stabilisation" of at least six months.
Earlier, IMI said it had empowered its executive committee to pursue negotiations which could lead to IMI becoming a core shareholder of San Paolo.
Currently, a foundation indirectly holds 65 percent of San Paolo, but this is planned to be reduced to 25 percent by offering shares to the public and a group of core shareholders.
IMI currently holds a two percent stake in San Paolo and has an option which expires in June to raise its stake to five percent.
